markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize **a small gated recent-interest residual with uniform multi-negative candidate cross-entropy**, evaluated through a controlled factorial comparison. Retain objective-only and simpler residual alternatives; do not presume the combined model wins. No validation improvement is established.

### Insights and directions

Three starting-point insights guide the proposal. First, user feedback identifies stale-history dominance; a causal recent-interest branch could represent current activity while retaining SASRec’s historical context. This is a hypothesis: history perturbations completed no users. Second, broad resemblance often lacks a concrete reason to choose; an asymmetric recent-item projection can learn directional next-item associations, but succession does not establish compatibility, complementarity or nonredundancy. Third, Electronics has 20.2% sampled training ranking errors and a −0.7499 tenth-percentile margin. These limited in-sample measurements motivate stronger candidate discrimination without predicting validation gains.

Three literature insights sharpen the experiment. [TLSRec](https://yneversky.github.io/Papers/cikm22.pdf) supports gated local/global fusion, but uses dimension-wise convex fusion rather than the proposed additive residual; it establishes neither a five-item window nor optimal initialization here. [Dross Into Gold](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07602) motivates multi-negative candidate CE, while [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) motivates separately testing generalized BCE. [Fossil](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152) and [SComGNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) motivate recent transitions and distinguishing complementarity from similarity, respectively; neither supplies missing compatibility labels.

### Framework

| Direction | Existing approach | Minimal experiment | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context | SASRec; TLSRec; Fossil | Gated recent residual | Current intent unobserved; simpler residual may suffice |
| Objective | BCE; gBCE; candidate CE | Uniform candidate CE | Negative count and loss formulation are separate factors; false negatives remain |
| Relations | Complementary graphs | Asymmetric recent projection | Compatibility and substitution labels absent |

### Candidate assessment

Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives one strength (+) and limitation (−). U/M denote user/model diagnosis alignment; alignment scores describe mechanisms, not demonstrated improvements.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | U | M | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform CE only | 2: +clean experiment; −established | 7: +reusable; −sampling-sensitive | 4: +sharper competition; −no explicit recency mechanism | 8: +targets separation; −in-sample evidence | 3: +small objective change; −correct sampling requires care |
| Recent residual only | 3: +compact adaptation; −strong precedents | 6: +current context; −fixed window can mix intents | 8: +current specific transitions; −no compatibility guarantee | 5: +additional signal; −separation uncertain | 3: +small branch; −scale and predictor synchronization |
| **Combined** | 3: +diagnosis-guided combination; −incremental components | 7: +tests complementary mechanisms; −unmeasured generalization | 8: +targets stale history and broad matches; −redundancy unresolved | 8: +candidate discrimination; −training errors may not predict HR@10 | 4: +modular implementation; −four configurations and coordinated artifacts |

The earlier combined originality/potential scores of 4/8 were optimistic given TLSRec, Fossil and established CE training; difficulty 4 remains reasonable. Other eligible directions remain useful controls rather than grounds for a larger immediate search.

### Selected algorithm

Preserve baseline normalization. At every valid position, average the raw tied item embeddings from the last five nonpadding positions, apply a bias-free asymmetric projection, and add a scalar gated residual to the normalized SASRec feature. This targets two user-facing failures: older isolated interactions outweighing current activity, and broad associations displacing specific current connections. Candidate CE targets Electronics’ observed sampled separation weakness. These are testable mechanisms, not guarantees against redundant devices, incompatible specifications or mismatched mood.

```text
r[t] = sum(raw_item_embedding(sequence[j]) for valid j in t−4…t)
       / max(1, number_of_valid_positions)
h[t] = unchanged_normalized_sasrec_feature[t]
g[t] = sigmoid(wᵀ concat(h[t], r[t]) + b)
f[t] = h[t] + g[t] * W r[t]
loss = mean_valid_positions CE(dot(f[t], embedding([positive[t], N_user])), 0)
```

Use a scalar gate with zero-initialized weights and bias −2, and a nonzero Xavier-initialized projection. This starts the gate near 0.12 while retaining a gradient path to it. Raw tied embeddings differ from SASRec inputs scaled by √d; report the measured residual/base norm ratio rather than assuming compatible scales. Do not normalize after addition in the primary comparison.

For each training sequence, sample K=min(64, eligible unseen count) unique uniform negatives without replacement, excluding padding and every known training interaction, including its targets. Share this set across the sequence’s positions; do not share it across users. Construct eligibility inside the user-aware training sampler before emitting the required `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` loader tuple; preserve user identity internally. Skip and count sequences with no eligible negatives. Use only training histories for exclusions. Training-seen exclusions define the objective’s support and may remove valid alternatives; unobserved false negatives remain. Apply no LogQ correction: this is candidate CE, not an estimator of full-catalog softmax [LogQ](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331).

Predeclare four complete configurations: unchanged SASRec, CE-only, residual-only and combined. The objective factor changes both negative count and loss, so its contrast identifies that package, not CE alone. If the remaining budget permits an explicitly preregistered extension, add K-negative BCE using identical negative draws and separately averaged positive/negative terms; add gBCE only as another separately budgeted control. Simpler last-item, ungated five-item and learned scalar residuals are follow-up controls, keeping projection and scale comparable.

Fix seeds 0/42, the effective 200-epoch default, optimizer settings, training positions and checkpoint rule before validation. Use the baseline checkpoint-selection rule unchanged, record it and every attempted configuration, and select by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, allowing baseline to win. Profile training cost and reserve diagnostic time before launching; the supplied remaining shared budget is unknown, so four-run feasibility cannot be assumed. Never exceed the shared 43,200 GPU-second limit.

When the host exposes paired hit vectors, retain identical evaluation users/candidates and bootstrap users within each category, preserving configuration pairing, then average categories equally. Report category differences, discordant wins/losses and the factorial interaction HR11−HR10−HR01+HR00. If vectors are unavailable, report scalar results without invented intervals or evaluator changes. Intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidates; they exclude training-seed variability. Predeclare a practical threshold and stopping rule, record all trials, and treat selected validation gains as exploratory because repeated selection is optimistic [Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/cawley10a/cawley10a.pdf).

Preserve all four models and routing, `DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']`, single-GPU execution, unchanged splits and trial-local artifacts. Synchronize checkpoint configuration, predictor generation and diagnostic hooks. Retain both required diagnostic callables and the actual trained module; expose fused features and consistent scoring, explicit dataset routing, measured definitions and unavailable probes as unknown. Monitor residual scale, gate saturation and matched sampled ranking errors; mean embedding alignment does not establish collapse or diversity. Titles/descriptions and timestamps remain optional public inputs; unavailable metadata, reviews, pretrained weights and simulator traits remain excluded.

idea.description: Evaluate a small scalar-gated, asymmetrically projected five-item recent-interest residual with uncorrected uniform multi-negative candidate cross-entropy in per-dataset SASRec. Use a four-configuration factorial comparison and retain the best completed configuration, including baseline.
idea.motivation: The causal recent branch explicitly targets older isolated interactions outweighing current activity and broad resemblance displacing specific current connections. Candidate CE addresses the measured Electronics sampled training separation weakness. These mechanisms do not establish compatibility, complementarity, ownership redundancy or validation improvement.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain separate models and explicit routing for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl; unchanged splits; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; the effective SASREC_EPOCHS default 200; and single-GPU execution. Preserve baseline normalization and optimizer settings in the primary comparison. Pool raw tied item embeddings causally over positions t−4 through t, masking padding and dividing by valid count. Add a bias-free Xavier-initialized projection through a scalar gate whose weights start at zero and bias at −2; do not zero the projection or add post-fusion normalization. Measure residual/base feature norm ratios and gate saturation. Within the user-aware sampler, draw up to 64 unique uniform negatives without replacement from items outside the user's complete training history, excluding padding. Share negatives across positions within that user's sequence; retain identity internally while preserving the required loader tuple. Skip and count empty eligible pools; never inspect withheld histories for exclusions. CE averages over valid positions, with an uncorrected denominator containing the target and sampled candidates. This is a candidate objective, not full-catalog softmax estimation. Predeclare the four baseline/objective/residual/combined configurations and record checkpoint selection, all attempts, practical selection threshold and stopping rule before querying validation. The objective contrast combines negative count and loss changes; add matched K-negative BCE only if separately budgeted, using identical draws and separately averaged positive and negative terms. Profile runtime, account for failed trials and diagnostics, and launch only configurations fitting the actual remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Select by pinned macro validation HR@10, allowing baseline to win. Use paired hit-vector analysis only if the host exposes outcomes; never alter its evaluator. Save architecture configuration, checkpoints and matching predictor beneath the trial directory. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis); expose view.model as the trained module, fused log2feats and consistent predict_score, explicit dataset routing, measured metric definitions and unknown values for unsupported probes. Do not infer diversity from embedding alignment, or compatibility from succession. Use only permitted public data and no external pretrained weights.
idea.pseudocode:
preregister_configs_and_checkpoint_rule()
profile_cost_and_check_actual_remaining_shared_budget()
for variant in budget_feasible_preregistered_variants:
    for category in FOUR_REQUIRED_CATEGORIES:
        initialize_category_training(seed=42)
        for epoch in configured_epochs(default=200):
            for user_aware_training_batch in sampler:
                sequence, positive, baseline_negative = unchanged_training_positions()
                h = unchanged_normalized_sasrec_features(sequence)
                if variant.uses_residual:
                    r = causal_valid_mean(raw_item_emb(sequence), window=5)
                    g = sigmoid(gate(concat(h, r)))
                    features = h + g * projection(r)
                else:
                    features = h
                if variant.uses_ce:
                    N = unique_uniform_training_unseen_items_per_user(K_up_to=64)
                    share_N_across_positions_within_each_sequence()
                    loss = mean_valid_candidate_CE(features, positive, N)
                else:
                    loss = unchanged_baseline_BCE(features, positive, baseline_negative)
                optimize(loss)
        apply_preregistered_baseline_checkpoint_rule()
        save_configuration_and_matching_checkpoint(category)
    write_matching_predictor_with_all_four_routes()
    obtain_pinned_macro_validation_HR10()
    cache_paired_hits_only_if_exposed_by_host()
select_best_completed_configuration_including_baseline()
report_category_deltas_and_factorial_interaction_when_all_four_complete()
report_paired_bootstrap_only_if_paired_hits_are_available()

originality.positive: The diagnosis-guided combination connects recent context and candidate discrimination to distinct failures and enables factorial attribution.
originality.negative: Recent-item transitions, local/global gating and multi-negative CE already have strong precedents; the architectural contribution is incremental.

future_potential.positive: Controlled results could motivate adaptive context selection and establish whether recent-context modeling complements objective changes.
future_potential.negative: Gains remain unmeasured; a fixed window can mix intents, and the method lacks evidence for compatibility or redundancy reasoning.

code_difficulty.positive: The model branch and candidate objective require modest, modular SASRec changes.
code_difficulty.negative: User-aware unique sampling, budget management, predictor generation, diagnostics and reproducible comparisons require coordinated implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the required causal self-attention baseline and tied item-embedding scoring.
Its implementation distinguishes scaled Transformer input embeddings from raw item embeddings and normalized output features.
limitations: The baseline does not establish solutions to the supplied user-facing failures.
Interaction embeddings do not establish functional compatibility.

related_work.title: TLSRec
contributions: Supports local/global interest modeling through dimension-wise, time-conditioned convex fusion.
limitations: Its fusion differs from the proposed additive residual.
It establishes neither the proposed window and initialization nor matched RecHarness improvements.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Combines increased negative sampling with generalized BCE to address sampled-training overconfidence.
limitations: Generalized BCE differs from candidate CE.
Its findings do not establish the best objective for this benchmark.

related_work.title: Turning Dross Into Gold Loss
contributions: Motivates full-softmax and multi-negative candidate cross-entropy for sequential recommendation.
Uses training-unseen sampled negatives shared across sequence positions.
limitations: Negative count, replacement policy and objective formulation require controlled comparison.
Observed exclusions cannot eliminate unobserved false negatives.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Clarifies corrections for approximating full-catalog softmax when the positive is deterministically included.
limitations: Correction cannot recover items outside the sampler's support.
Uncorrected training-unseen candidate CE should not be described as full-catalog softmax estimation.

related_work.title: Fossil
contributions: Combines item similarity with weighted recent-item transitions, motivating simple recent-history controls.
limitations: Does not establish the benefit of a learned gate or a five-item window in this benchmark.

related_work.title: SComGNN
contributions: Motivates distinguishing complementary relationships from simple similarity.
limitations: Training-history succession cannot be treated as verified complementarity.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains optimism introduced by repeated model selection using finite validation data.
limitations: Paired uncertainty intervals do not remove adaptive selection bias or substitute for independent training runs.

related_work.title: SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling suitable for preserving configuration outcomes within users.
limitations: Requires paired outcomes exposed by the host.
User resampling conditions on fitted models and fixed candidate sets.

related_work.title: NIST factorial design guidance
contributions: Supports full factorial comparisons and explicit treatment of confounding and interactions.
limitations: Four configurations isolate the declared architecture and objective-package factors, not the separate effects of negative count and loss.
